what: An audit of the remakes decision test (statistics and the size of the effect) from committed outputs only; made by results/v2/second/audit/statistics.py. Each number has 'what' (one line) and 'source' (the committed file and key path it comes from, or the inputs it was computed from).

files.what: the committed files this audit read

T_from_family_sums_minus_committed.what: sum of family_sums.rows D minus slope.T

T_from_entries_minus_committed.what: sum of entries_table contributions minus slope.T

Z_recomputed_minus_committed.what: T / sqrt(sum of D squared) minus slope.Z

largest_gap_family_sum_vs_its_entries.what: largest absolute difference between a family's D and the sum of its entries' contributions

largest_gap_open_mass_vs_its_entries.what: largest absolute difference between a family's open_mass and the sum of (1 - words probability) of its entries

effective_number_of_families_recomputed_.what: (sum |D|)^2 / sum D^2 minus the committed value

subsets_recomputed_largest_gap.what: largest absolute difference, over the eleven committed subsets and their fields (entries, families, T, Z, positive, negative, open pairs), between the committed value and the value recomputed from entries_table (the Z of the copied subset left aside: see copied_subset_Z)

subset_sign_flip_p_recomputed_and_commit.what: each subset's sign-flip p recomputed with the registered seed and draws, beside the committed p

copied_subset_Z.what: the copied subset's Z (-1.41 in the file) is a ratio of rounding residues near 1e-13: it is 0/0 and carries no information

adds_up__not_copied__plus__copied.what: committed T, entries and open pairs of the two complementary subsets, added and compared with all entries

adds_up__recognised__plus__not_recognise.what: committed T, entries and open pairs of the two complementary subsets, added and compared with all entries

adds_up__recognised_both_films__plus__no.what: committed T, entries and open pairs of the two complementary subsets, added and compared with all entries

adds_up__source_is_a_document_of_v2_refe.what: committed T, entries and open pairs of the two complementary subsets, added and compared with all entries

largest_families_left_out_gap.what: largest |T without the family + the family's sum - T|, five families

decision_block_equals_the_analysis.what: decision.slope, decision.gain and decision.recall_rule equal the same blocks of the primary analysis

stand_ins_largest_Z_three_places.what: the stand-ins' largest Z in the words file, in the decision block and in the noise file

noise_file_rates_recomputed.what: the noise draws' share of Z above the stand-ins' largest Z and the standard deviation of Z, recomputed from Z_sorted (rounded to 4 places)

recognition_flags_equal_the_recognition_.what: entries_table's two recognition flags equal the 'pairs' rows of the recognition file

entries_that_disagree_with_pairs_json.what: entries whose family, copied flag, block or wording differ from pairs.json (none expected)

counts_of_the_primary_set_against_the_pl.what: the primary set's counts recomputed from entries_table, beside PLAN.md Section 15 (220 pairs, 217 remakes, 185 sources, 175 families, 100 copied, 96 under 1%, 137 reference sources)

families_counted_as_non_zero_that_are_ro.what: '47 positive against 57 negative' counts every family whose sum is not exactly 0.0; this many of the 104 are zero to within 1e-6 (the word model is certain of the source and the sum is a rounding residue)

largest_families_removed_one_after_anoth.what: T, Z, sign-flip p (registered seed) and noise-calibrated p after the k families with the largest sums are removed, k = 0 to 20 (the noise draws are of the whole list, so the last column is a guide after removals)

noise_Z_95th_percentile.what: 95th percentile of Z over the 2,000 pure-noise draws

families_to_remove_for_Z_under_the_stand.what: smallest k for which Z falls below the stand-ins' largest Z (2.2280)

families_to_remove_for_Z_under_the_noise.what: smallest k for which Z falls below the 95th percentile of the pure-noise Z

families_to_remove_for_sign_flip_p_at_or.what: smallest k for which the sign-flip p is 0.05 or more

families_to_remove_for_T_at_or_below_zer.what: smallest k for which the sum is no longer positive

leave_one_family_out_Z_range.what: smallest and largest Z when any single family is left out

family_sums_winsorised.what: the family sums clipped to plus or minus c: T, Z, sign-flip p, noise-calibrated p

entry_contributions_winsorised.what: the entries' contributions clipped to plus or minus c before the family sums: T, Z, sign-flip p, noise-calibrated p

share_of_T_in_the_largest_families.what: share of T held by the k largest family sums

share_of_sum_of_squares_in_the_largest_f.what: share of the sum of squared family sums held by the k largest

reboot_in_the_statement.what: the stating sentence contains 'reboot' (Section 3 lists it among the loose words)

decided_by_a_third_reader.what: the two readers differed on a statement of the pair

two_steps_from_the_source.what: pairs.json also holds (remake, m) and (m, source) for some film m: the entry's source is the original two steps back

table_year_contradicts_the_statement.what: every year on the remake's own stating sentences differs from the table's year of the source by more than 2

stated_only_off_the_remakes_page.what: no stating sentence is on the remake's own page

any_of_reboot_third_reader_two_steps_or_.what: any of the four flags above that bear on what the pair is

pairs_whose_statement_is_contestable.what: the primary entries by what is unusual in pairs.json about them: how many, which of them the words leave open, their share of T, and the test without them (their contributions set to zero; nothing refitted)

by_shortest_text.what: the contributions summed over pairs whose shorter text has at least 20 sentences, and over the rest (nothing refitted)

noise_calibrated_p.what: share of the 2,000 pure-noise draws whose Z is at or above the units' Z, the observed value counted as one; no draw reaches it, so 0.0005 is the smallest value this can take

noise_normal_extrapolations.what: the observed Z and T set against the noise draws' standard deviations (normal tail areas; the noise Z has sd 1.24 where sign flips assume 1)

value.strongest_generator: TF-IDF on a random half of the words

against_word_only_measures.what: the units' Z set against every word-only measure whose Z is committed: the 74 stand-ins and the 332 random word-only measures (none reaches it; the best has Z 3.12), with normal tail areas from the mean and sd of all random measures and of the generator with the heaviest upper tail

five_lowest_p_and_their_settings: mean of the word columns | minus log rank | noise 1
one random word column | signed square | noise 0.5
one random word column | tanh(x/3) | noise 0.5
random signed mix of the word columns | cube | noise 1
random signed mix of the word columns | normal score of the rank | noise 0

against_noisy_and_curved_copies.what: the noisy and curved copies of the word columns: only rates and each setting's lowest p are committed (no Z), so the units' Z cannot be set against the copies' largest Z; one setting's lowest p is at the floor of its 5,000 flips (0.0002) and the next lowest is 0.0006

bootstrap_mean_family_sum.what: bootstrap over the 175 families of the mean family sum (T / 175): percentile and BCa intervals, and the share of resamples with a mean at or below zero

bootstrap_effect_per_open_pair.what: T divided by the effective open pairs (normal-score units by which the source's unit rank beats what the word model expects, per pair the words leave open), with a family bootstrap

bootstrap_mean_family_sum_open_families_.what: the same bootstrap over only the families with more than a tenth of a pair open

sign_and_signed_rank_tests.what: positive and negative family sums, the one-sided sign test and Wilcoxon signed-rank test, by the size of the sum and by how much of a pair the family leaves open

distribution_of_the_family_sums.what: the shape of the 175 family sums: a few large positive sums, almost no negative sum of any size

what_the_sign_flip_p_amounts_to.what: T is 91% of the largest value any sign pattern could give, so the registered p is in effect the chance that the 16 or so sizeable sums nearly all come out positive

sources_ranked_first.what: how often the true source is ranked first among its candidates: by the held-out word model, by the hub-corrected unit rate alone, and by the word model refitted with the unit column

pairs_the_word_model_gets_wrong.what: the 15 pairs whose source the word model does not rank first: where the units alone rank it

T_by_whether_the_word_model_ranks_the_so.what: T split by whether the word model ranks the true source first: the 15 pairs it gets wrong hold most of T and every one of their contributions is positive; the registered p is close to the chance of 15 signs out of 15

pairs_the_word_model_gets_right.what: the 205 pairs whose source the word model ranks first: where the units alone rank it

mean_reciprocal_rank.what: mean reciprocal rank of the true source by the word model and by the units alone (the last line takes, pair by pair, the better of the two ranks: an upper bound no rule could reach without knowing the answer)

the_refitted_model.what: what the committed gain block says about the word model refitted with the unit column: 19.6 nats of held-out log-likelihood, one more source ranked first (205 to 206)

pairs_the_words_leave_more_than_half_ope.what: the 20 entries where the word model gives the true source a probability under 0.5: where the units alone rank the source

effect_in_the_test_s_own_unit.what: T per open pair (about 1.2 normal-score units) beside the smallest planted boost the test finds with 80% power, in pool standard deviations

units_alone_against_words_alone_heredity.what: on the 120 pairs that are not copied the units alone rank the source first in 76, the word model in 105

splits.what: every summary by recognition (the wide rule used by condition 7, and the narrower one): T, Z, sign-flip p, open pairs, T per open pair, sources first by words and by units; the noise-calibrated p uses the whole list's noise draws and is only a guide for a subset

not_recognised_largest_families_removed.what: condition 7's statistic after the k largest family sums of the unrecognised entries are removed

not_recognised_families_to_remove_for_p_.what: smallest k for which condition 7's p is 0.05 or more

not_recognised_concentration.what: how concentrated the unrecognised entries' sum is

recognised_minus_not_per_open_pair.what: T per open pair among recognised entries minus the same among unrecognised entries, with a family bootstrap
